language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Nike's FY27 guide assumed incremental tariffs of 10% through July then 15% thereafter, but when Section 122 expired on 2026-07-24 it was replaced by a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% depending on the country (Vietnam at 12.5%), so the rate on goods landing from August is 2.5-5 points below plan, a gross-margin tailwind that can only show up in the Q2/H2 margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-06-30): fell ~8% after hours on the cautious Q1 outlook and closed +4.9% once the call pulled gross-margin expansion forward to Q1 (sweep row, CNBC); margin-timing has been the line that reversed the last reaction.

findings.finding: Nike's largest North American wholesale partners reported sell-through weakness over the June-August window after Nike last spoke: JD Sports North America like-for-like -6.8% in the 13 weeks to 1 August with Nike over 40% of JD's sales and a profit-guide cut, and Foot Locker comps -3.6% at Dick's, blamed on legacy and retro footwear and an increasingly promotional market; BofA's downgrade cites the gap between Nike's NA wholesale growth and sell-through, which points at a softer Q2/H2 sell-in guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-03-31) beat and fell -15.5% close-to-close on a weak Q4 guide; Q2 FY26 (2025-12-18) fell -10.5% — the guide is what this name trades on.

findings.finding: China retail kept falling through the quarter: Pou Sheng (Yue Yuen's China retail arm, a Nike and Adidas reseller) posted August revenue -9% y/y and Topsports' March-May sales fell by a low-teens percentage, while Nike's own termination of online authorisations for thousands of China resellers from 2027-01-01 adds a headwind to the H2 China guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2025-12-18) fell -10.5% with China cited as the drag; Q4 FY26 China -17% did not stop a +4.9% close.

findings.finding: Street Q2 EPS of $0.53 already sits on the ceiling of Nike's own 'flattish earnings ex-tariff-recovery' framework for Q4 FY26-Q2 FY27 (prior-year $0.14 + $0.49 + $0.53 = $1.16; Q4 FY26 ex-benefit delivered $0.20, so Q1+Q2 needs ~$0.96 against consensus $0.44 + $0.53 = $0.97), while Nike pre-flagged a multipoint sequential revenue deceleration into Q2 and UBS expects an implied Q2 of $0.31-0.43.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: beat, guide below Street, -15.5%; Q4 FY26: guide composition shifted (revenue lower, margin earlier), AH -8% then +4.9% close.

findings.finding: The bar has been cut hard into the print — Baird to Neutral (PT $70 to $44), BofA to Underperform ($30), Morgan Stanley Underweight ($31), BMO Underperform ($30), Piper, Citi, UBS, Telsey and Evercore ($34) target cuts, S&P 100 removal on 2026-09-21 — with record short interest of ~87M shares, while Jefferies (2026-09-28) expects a Q1 beat at $11.5bn / $0.48.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-06-30): a de-rated name with a cautious guide reversed from -8% after hours to +4.9%; Q1 FY26 (2025-09-30) +6.4%.

outside_window.finding: Nike ends online sales authorisation for China resellers (incl. Topsports, ~RMB5.6bn of its annual sales) effective 2027-01-01; the revenue effect lands in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Remaining ~$686m of the $986m IEEPA refund was a receivable at 2026-05-31 (over $300m collected); collection is cash and balance-sheet only, not P&L.
